alerts.title: Overdue serum creatinine monitoring on TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring every 12 months for patients on TDF. The patient's last creatinine was 478 days ago (2024-10-01), exceeding the 12-month interval. TDF can cause chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and Fanconi syndrome. No renal monitoring was ordered at today's visit. The prior creatinine of 88 umol/L was normal, but no current renal function data is available to assess ongoing TDF safety.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR now; ensure annual renal monitoring is scheduled for all patients on TDF-based ART.

alerts.title: Low-level viremia on current regimen
alerts.message: Guidelines define viral suppression as plasma ≤200 copies/mL but note that low-level viremia above the detection threshold warrants attention. The patient's latest viral load is 40 copies/mL (2025-10-01), which is suppressed but detectable. Persistent low-level viremia can be associated with risk of subsequent virologic non-suppression. The clinician's plan does not address this detectable result. Repeat viral load testing per routine annual schedule is indicated to confirm ongoing suppression.

evidence.recommended_action: Continue routine annual viral load monitoring; consider repeat VL at next visit to confirm sustained suppression given detectable low-level result.
